payload.name: Disambiguate creation dates from sharing memories
payload.description: When a question asks when someone made or created a named item and retrieval returns only sharing, mentioning, or favoriting memories, search for event memories of making/testing/creating before answering.
content: If a question asks when someone made/created a specific dish or item, treat only event memories describing the act of making, testing, baking, creating, cooking, or trying as evidence of the creation date; memories of sharing, mentioning, or liking the item reflect when it was discussed, not made.

After the first search, if the only explicit matches are sharing, preference, or plan memories, run a follow-up search for the person combined with creation verbs (made, tested, baked, created, cooked, tried) and generic descriptors (new recipe, treat, dessert, dish, project) without requiring the exact item name.

If a retrieved event memory describes a generic creation by the same person near a plausible time but omits the item name, inspect its source context to determine whether it refers to the asked-about item before using its date.
Stop once an event memory directly or via source context confirms the creation date, or after the creation-focused search returns no same-subject event; do not keep expanding indefinitely.

solves: Questions that ask when someone made or created a specific item often fail because retrieval returns memories where the item was shared, mentioned, or favored, and the agent mistakes those timestamps for the creation date. The actual creation event may be stored with generic wording (e.g., 'tested a new recipe') and is missed by keyword searches for the exact item name.
